fields.notes: TPM 2.0 deliberately exposes no scan / JTAG / boundary-scan path on the host interface — exposure of internal state on a scan chain would invalidate the security model. All host-visible DFT is via the Part-3 commands listed above. Vendor wafer / package test uses a separate internal debug port that is fused / locked before release.

exposed_dft_features.name: TPM2_SelfTest
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Run full or incremental self-test over implemented algorithms.

exposed_dft_features.name: TPM2_GetCapability(TPM_CAP_ALGS)
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Lists which algorithms have completed self-test.

exposed_dft_features.name: TPM_STS.selfTestDone bit
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Sticky bit; clears when a self-test is in progress.

exposed_dft_features.name: TPM2_SetCommandCodeAuditStatus
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Track all uses of a sensitive command for compliance audit.

exposed_dft_features.name: TPM2_GetCommandAuditDigest
exposed_dft_features.purpose: Sign and return the command-audit digest.

fields.no_jtag_on_host_interface: There is no JTAG, no boundary-scan, no debug-UART on the TPM host pins. Any such path would have to be cryptographically gated and is not in the public spec.
fields.side_channel_hardening_obligation: Implementations are required by the TPM Protection Profile to harden against timing, power, and fault-injection side channels. Specific countermeasures (balanced logic, blinding, masking, random delay, repeat-then-compare) are vendor-defined.
